governance.status: ANALYTICAL LITERATURE REVIEW — HYPOTHESES NOT YET PROJECT-VALIDATED
governance.description: Audited Literature Map v2: Forensic audit of all citations, explicit claim support classification, removal of misattributions, and addition of structure-preserving and output-specific foundations.

literature_entries.authors: McKeon, B. J.; Sharma, A. S.
literature_entries.title: A critical-layer framework for turbulent pipe flow
literature_entries.problem_studied: Input-output formulation of wall-bounded shear flows; singular value decomposition of linearized Navier-Stokes resolvent operator around turbulent mean velocity profile.
literature_entries.method: Resolvent analysis treating nonlinear advection terms as an unknown forcing and velocity/pressure as the linear response.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Rank-1 resolvent response modes capture primary energetic coherent structures, critical layers, and wall-attached velocity scaling.
literature_entries.limitations: Linearized around an empirical turbulent mean profile; requires mean profile knowledge; does not provide standalone closed dynamical system without nonlinear feedback closure.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly supports our Candidate W9-G ResolventResponseBasis for input-output response gain analysis, near-wall energetic structures, and wall-shear observable sensitivity. Does NOT support standalone closed-loop time-stepping ROM without closure.
literature_entries.project_inference: Our channel-flow discrete staggered operators can compute these input-output resolvent response modes directly.

literature_entries.authors: Toedtli, S. S.; Luhar, M.; McKeon, B. J.
literature_entries.title: Predicting the response of turbulent channel flow to varying-phase opposition control: resolvent analysis as a tool for flow control design
literature_entries.problem_studied: Prediction of turbulent channel flow response to active opposition boundary control and drag reduction.
literature_entries.method: Resolvent-based transfer function gain analysis relating wall blowing/suction actuation to wall shear stress modification.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Successfully predicted optimal sensor placement and phase shift for wall shear reduction without requiring full DNS parametric sweeps.
literature_entries.limitations: Assumes mean profile distortion is predictable or small; validated for boundary actuation in channel geometry.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct precedent for using resolvent modes as an output-specific tool for wall-shear sensitivity and active control design.
literature_entries.project_inference: We can test whether our discrete MAC-staggered resolvent code reproduces the qualitative gain structure for wall actuation without claiming project-validated drag reduction.

literature_entries.authors: Schlegel, M.; Noack, B. R.; Jordan, P.; Dillmann, A.; Gröschel, E.; Schröder, W.; Wei, M.; Freund, J. B.; Lehmann, O.; Tadmor, G.
literature_entries.title: On least-order flow representations for aerodynamics and aeroacoustics
literature_entries.problem_studied: Constructing reduced-order representations targeted at specific linear observables (lift, drag, far-field acoustic pressure) rather than global kinetic energy.
literature_entries.method: Observable Inferred Decomposition (OID): generalized Galerkin expansion isolating least-residual modes (state estimation) and least-energetic modes (control gain) for specific goal functionals.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Reduces mode count by over an order of magnitude when predicting specific aerodynamic observables (lift/drag on cylinder wake, acoustic radiation from mixing layers and jets) compared to standard energy-norm POD.
literature_entries.limitations: Linear functional observables; modes optimized for one observable may have poor global L2 state accuracy.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct precedent for our project observation that wall-shear stress error (E_tau_w approx 3.9%) can be low while full-state velocity error (E_u approx 28%) is high. Validates goal-oriented modal reduction.
literature_entries.project_inference: Our DerivativeWeightedStokesBasis and SeparableChannelEigenbasis operate as empirical observable-specific bases targeted at the wall shear functional.

literature_entries.title: On long-term stability of POD-Galerkin models of a plane mixing layer
literature_entries.problem_studied: Energy conservation and long-term boundedness of linear-quadratic Galerkin reduced-order models of fluid flow.
literature_entries.method: Analysis of quadratic interaction tensor symmetries; proving that preserving skew-symmetry of the nonlinear convection tensor is necessary to prevent unphysical energy growth.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Enforcing exact skew-symmetry on modal quadratic tensors Q_kij guarantees energy boundedness in the absence of viscosity; identifying that ad-hoc truncation of quadratic terms destroys conservation.
literature_entries.limitations: Focuses on Galerkin systems derived from snapshot POD; requires subgrid dissipation for correct physical decay rate.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly explains our W5/W7 negative result (N04/N06): heuristic truncation of weak triads destroyed tensor skew-symmetry, causing catastrophic energy blowup. Validates our SparseModalTensor skew-symmetrization.
literature_entries.project_inference: Our OnTheFlyFFTEvaluator succeeded because it evaluates the full continuous skew-symmetric operator on a collocation grid, avoiding truncation entirely. (Our FFT solver is independent project evidence).

literature_entries.authors: Reiss, J.; Schulze, P.; Sesterhenn, J.; Mehrmann, V.
literature_entries.title: The Shifted Proper Orthogonal Decomposition: A mode decomposition for multiple transport phenomena
literature_entries.venue: SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing, 40(3), A1322-A1344
literature_entries.problem_studied: Failure of classical linear POD on transport-dominated problems, moving shocks, and traveling waves (slow Kolmogorov n-width decay).
literature_entries.method: Shifted POD (sPOD): decomposing fields into superpositions of comoving frames with time-dependent spatial shifts c_k(t).
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Achieves order-of-magnitude mode reduction for 1D/2D traveling waves, acoustic pulses, and advecting vortices compared to standard POD.
literature_entries.limitations: Tested primarily on isolated transport phenomena and 1D/2D wave equations; shift optimization is non-convex for complex multi-scale turbulent eddies.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Supports shifted modal decomposition for transport-dominated phenomena. Does NOT prove that cross-seed turbulent failure is purely a 1D shift issue.
literature_entries.project_inference: IF cross-seed difference in homogeneous directions is dominated by spatial translations, THEN symmetry reduction / alignment will reduce subspace distance (to be tested via R_align pretest).

literature_entries.authors: Rowley, C. W.; Marsden, J. E.
literature_entries.title: Reconstruction equations and the Karhunen-Loève expansion for systems with symmetry
literature_entries.problem_studied: Model reduction of dynamical systems exhibiting continuous Lie group symmetries (translations, rotations).
literature_entries.method: Symmetry reduction / slicing method: projecting dynamics onto a quotient space orthogonal to group orbits before computing POD.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Reduces dimension of traveling-wave attractors by removing phase drift degrees of freedom.
literature_entries.limitations: Requires explicit group parameterization; requires solving auxiliary reconstruction ODE for phase velocity.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct mathematical foundation for factoring out spatial translation group actions in periodic homogeneous directions (x, z).
literature_entries.project_inference: Our W4 optimal_translation_alignment is a discrete grid search over the translation group orbit.

literature_entries.authors: Amsallem, D.; Zahr, M. J.; Farhat, C.
literature_entries.title: Nonlinear model order reduction based on local reduced-order bases
literature_entries.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering, 92(10), 891-916
literature_entries.problem_studied: Model reduction for nonlinear systems where single global linear subspace has high Kolmogorov n-width.
literature_entries.method: Partitioning snapshot manifold into clusters, constructing local POD bases per cluster, and online smooth basis switching.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Orders-of-magnitude reduction in online dimension and error for nonlinear shock propagation and structural contact.
literature_entries.limitations: Cluster boundary chattering requires hysteresis/smoothing; effective for systems with distinct localized operating regimes.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct precedent for our ClusteredLocalPODBasis (R08). Proves that local clustering is a standard method when global linear subspaces encounter high manifold curvature.
literature_entries.project_inference: Clustered local POD is better suited to multi-regime structural dynamics (bistable buckling) than continuous homogeneous turbulence.

literature_entries.authors: Kaiser, E.; Noack, B. R.; Cordier, L.; Spohn, A.; Segond, M.; Abel, M.; Brunton, S. L.; Östh, J.; Krajnović, S.; Niven, R. K.
literature_entries.title: Cluster-based reduced-order modelling of a jet in crossflow
literature_entries.problem_studied: Reduced-order modeling of strongly nonlinear, non-stationary fluid flows with multiple operating regimes and intermittency.
literature_entries.method: Cluster-based Reduced-Order Modeling (CROM): state-space k-means clustering combined with Markov transition models.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Captures multi-attractor switching and transition probabilities in a turbulent jet without continuous Galerkin ODE integration.
literature_entries.limitations: Statistical/probabilistic model; coarse spatial resolution determined by number of cluster centroids.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct precedent for transitioning failed continuous ROMs to discrete Markovian state transitions using snapshot clustering.
literature_entries.project_inference: Our snapshot clustering infrastructure can be used for discrete regime-transition modeling.

literature_entries.title: Divergence-free and curl-free wavelets in two dimensions and three dimensions: application to turbulent flows
literature_entries.problem_studied: Compactly supported divergence-free multiresolution wavelet bases for 2D/3D incompressible Navier-Stokes.
literature_entries.method: Multiresolution Analysis (MRA) constructing divergence-free wavelets with exact Helmholtz decomposition.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Exact solenoidality without pressure Poisson solve; efficient representation of localized turbulent structures.
literature_entries.limitations: Periodic or free-space boundary conditions; extension to non-periodic no-slip walls requires complex boundary wavelets.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Mathematical foundation for our W13-F / W13-G multiresolution solenoidal dictionaries.
literature_entries.project_inference: Explains why our periodic solenoidal wave packets are mathematically sound, while wall-normal boundary wavelets encounter conditioning issues.

literature_entries.title: Coherent vortex extraction in three-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence using orthogonal wavelets
literature_entries.problem_studied: Denoising and coherent structure extraction in 3D homogeneous turbulence.
literature_entries.method: Orthogonal wavelet thresholding separating coherent non-Gaussian vortex tubes from incoherent Gaussian noise.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Retaining ~3% of wavelet coefficients captures >99% of kinetic energy and all intermittency.
literature_entries.limitations: Static field extraction; forward dynamical evolution of sparse wavelet coefficients requires adaptive tree tracking.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct precedent for our SparsificationEngine participation ratio and effective dimension analysis.
literature_entries.project_inference: Our multiresolution solenoidal dictionary has genuine utility for static coherent vortex extraction and inverse sensor recovery, independent of forward ROM claims.

literature_entries.title: Fourth-order time-stepping for stiff PDEs
literature_entries.problem_studied: Stable, high-order time-stepping of stiff semilinear PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, reaction-diffusion, KdV).
literature_entries.method: Exponential Time Differencing 4th-order Runge-Kutta (ETDRK4) with complex contour integration for stable phi-function evaluation.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Enables timesteps 10x-100x larger than standard explicit schemes on stiff Laplacians.
literature_entries.limitations: Requires diagonal or efficiently factorizable linear operator; explicit step still constrained by nonlinear Lipschitz constant.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct foundation for our IntegratingFactorModalODEIntegrator (R13) and StokesEigenmodeODEIntegrator (W8).
literature_entries.project_inference: Our ETD implementation is a reliable software asset for semilinear PDEs with diagonal linear parts.

literature_entries.title: Exponential integrators
literature_entries.problem_studied: Comprehensive mathematical theory and error bounds for exponential time differencing across parabolic and hyperbolic PDEs.
literature_entries.method: Semigroup and sectorial operator theory for exponential multistep and Runge-Kutta methods.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Rigorous convergence proofs and stability bounds for stiff semilinear parabolic systems.
literature_entries.limitations: Comprehensive survey paper; theoretical bounds assume bounded nonlinearities.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Provides mathematical foundation for why our ETD implementation achieves machine-precision linear decay.
literature_entries.project_inference: ETD is mathematically proven for parabolic semilinear systems, making our cross-domain reaction-diffusion transfer a high-confidence software smoke test.

literature_entries.title: Properties of Ramanujan filter banks
literature_entries.problem_studied: Extraction of hidden integer periodicities in noisy discrete time series.
literature_entries.method: Ramanujan periodic transforms and orthogonal filter banks based on arithmetic Ramanujan sums c_q(n).
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Finite-duration extraction of integer-periodic components without spectral leakage.
literature_entries.limitations: Discrete arithmetic periodicities; not adapted to continuous spatial differential operators.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Explains why RamanujanCorrection failed for continuous spatial fluid turbulence (N13) while identifying its correct application domain in discrete time series.
literature_entries.project_inference: Ramanujan transforms should be permanently retired from continuous spatial fluid modeling.

literature_entries.authors: Carlberg, K.; Farhat, C.; Cortial, J.; Amsallem, D.
literature_entries.title: The GNAT method for nonlinear model reduction of large-scale computational models
literature_entries.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering, 86(2), 155-181
literature_entries.problem_studied: Nonlinear model reduction and hyper-reduction for large-scale engineering systems using Gauss-Newton with optimal truncation (GNAT).
literature_entries.method: Petrov-Galerkin projection minimizing nonlinear residual over low-dimensional trial subspace using gappy sample mesh.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Order-of-magnitude speedup with preserved stability on large-scale compressible CFD and structural problems.
literature_entries.limitations: Requires offline training trajectories and gappy mesh selection; complex implementation.
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct literature foundation for Petrov-Galerkin residual minimization.
literature_entries.project_inference: Petrov-Galerkin is a distinct hyper-reduction and residual-minimizing method, separate from output-specific observable decomposition.

literature_entries.authors: Dudley, M. L.; James, I. N.
literature_entries.title: Time-dependent kinematic dynamos with stationary spherical flows
literature_entries.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A, 425(1869), 407-429
literature_entries.problem_studied: Kinematic dynamo magnetic field induction under prescribed stationary velocity fields.
literature_entries.method: Spectral expansion of solenoidal magnetic field B under prescribed incompressible flow u.
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Computed magnetic growth rates gamma and proved magnetic field amplification without Lorentz-force feedback.
literature_entries.limitations: Kinematic approximation: velocity field u is fixed and does not respond to magnetic Lorentz force (J x B = 0 assumed in momentum equation).
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct foundation for our Roberts-Flow Kinematic Induction/Dynamo Test (HYP-05).
literature_entries.project_inference: Our exact FourierSolenoidalBasis satisfies div B = 0 to machine precision, making it an ideal tool for kinematic dynamo eigenvalue calculations.
